name: יְהוּדָה
summary: Jacob’s fourth son by Leah, and the tribe that came from him, which camped first on the east and set out first of all, its host under Nahshon son of Amminadab (Num 2:3; 10:14), from which came David’s kings and the Christ (Gen 49:10; Heb 7:14); also Levites and others of the return in Ezra and Nehemiah. Leah named him from the hiphil of יָדָה: “This time I will praise Yahweh; therefore she called his name Judah” (Gen 29:35), and Jacob’s blessing plays on it again, “Judah, your brothers shall praise you” (Gen 49:8). How the name’s ה before the וּ is formed the text does not say; its meaning is the one these two verses give it. The gentilic יְהוּדִי, “man of Judah”, became the name “Jew”.

evidence.note: “She said, This time I will praise (אוֹדֶה) Yahweh; therefore she called his name יְהוּדָה.”
“יְהוּדָה אַתָּה יוֹדוּךָ אַחֶיךָ”: Judah, you, your brothers shall praise you.
“The sceptre shall not depart from Judah … until Shiloh comes, and to him shall be the obedience of the peoples.”
On the east, the standard of the camp of Judah, under Nahshon son of Amminadab.
“The standard of the camp of the sons of Judah set out first by their hosts, and over its host was Nahshon son of Amminadab.”
“It is evident that our Lord sprang out of Judah.”
“The lion of the tribe of Judah, the root of David, has prevailed.”
“He is a Jew who is one inwardly … whose praise is not from men but from God”: Paul plays on the name, as Gen 49:8 does.
“A man, a יְהוּדִי, in Shushan”: Mordecai, a Benjamite, called by the gentilic of Judah, “Jew”.
The Aramaic יְהוּדָיֵא, “the Jews”, accused before Nebuchadnezzar.
Judah, one of the Levites who had taken foreign wives.
Judah son of Hassenuah, second over the city.
Judah among the Levites of the return, with Mattaniah who was over the songs of thanksgiving (הֻיְּדוֹת).
Judah among the musicians at the dedication of the wall.

note: Takes j.av.ai (the name, 820 tokens, which includes the tribe and the land and kingdom of Judah, so its count is not all the person), the gentilic יְהוּדִי j.av.aj and the Aramaic gentilic יְהוּדַי xj.ad.ac, which TIPNR lists as forms of Judah@Gen.29.35. BDB files Judah under יהב, an artefact of its order; Gen 29:35 and 49:8 tie it to ידה. Left out: יְהוּדִית “in the Jews’ language” (j.av.ak, an adverb from the gentilic), the Aramaic land name יְהוּד (xj.ad.ab, a place), Jehudi (j.av.al) and Judith (j.av.am), who are other people. Judah@Luk.3.30 (Ἰούδα in Luke’s genealogy) and the New Testament’s Judas are not tagged: TIPNR gives them no Hebrew form. The tribe’s land (Judea@Ezr.9.9) is a place.
